Title: Anwar: TH investigations can go beyond RCI scope and cover developments up to 2025
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: Investigations into issues surrounding Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH) are not confined to the period covered by the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) and can extend beyond 2020, including developments up to 2025.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the RCI served as the main framework for examining issues involving TH, but enforcement and investigative agencies were not restricted from looking into matters that occurred before or after the period covered by the commission.
"It is not a proposal. All the actions and studies being undertaken now go beyond the RCI. The RCI serves as the main framework.
"There is no restriction on investigating matters before and after that period.
"This is what the enforcement and investigative agencies are doing," he said this when met after attending the 2027 Budget Engagement Session at the Finance Ministry here today.

Title: Probe launched after premature baby tests positive for prohibited substance
Article:
KOTA BARU: The Kelantan Welfare Department has launched an investigation after a urine test on a premature baby at a hospital detected the presence of a prohibited substance.
Its director, Che Samsuzuki Che Noh, said the department received a referral from the hospital last week after the baby, who required further treatment, underwent the urine screening.
He said the hospital also lodged a police report following the test result.
"The state welfare department, through our Child Protection Unit, immediately took action by obtaining information from the biological mother and conducting checks with the National Anti-Drug Agency (NADA).
"We also sought the police's assistance in the investigation.
"Initial checks found that the biological mother had no record with NADA," he said.
Che Samsuzuki said the department conducted further investigations on Aug 12 by visiting the family's home and interviewing the baby's biological mother and father.
He said several matters required further scrutiny, including information relating to the mother's consumption of medication and use of certain substances before the baby's birth.
"The case has also come to the attention of police for further investigation," he said.
He said the baby remained in hospital for treatment and was under the supervision of medical personnel.
Che Samsuzuki said the department would continue to obtain information, relevant documents and examination results from the hospital, police, NADA and other agencies to complete its investigation.
He said the assessment would focus on the safety, welfare and best interests of the child.
"The department will continue to coordinate with the relevant agencies and take appropriate follow-up action based on the findings of the investigation," he said.
It was
reported
that the Kelantan Health Department was monitoring a newborn girl who tested positive for amphetamines and benzodiazepines following a urine screening at the Raja Perempuan Zainab II Hospital (HRPZ II) Neonatal Intensive Care Unit (NICU) on Aug 6.
Deputy Health director Dr Rohana Daud said the mother was believed to have taken sedatives, prompting health officials to monitor the infant for withdrawal symptoms.

Title: Poor contractor management behind 75 per cent of delayed, sick projects - Ahmad Maslan
Article:
BUTTERWORTH: Poor contractor management, weak operational supervision and financial problems account for 75 per cent of delayed and "sick" projects nationwide.
Deputy Works Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Maslan said technical and construction site issues accounted for only 25 per cent of the problems.
This, he said, highlights the need for contractors to strengthen their management capabilities and financial position.
"Analysis showed that 75 per cent of disrupted projects stemmed from weaknesses in contractor management, poor operational supervision and financial problems.
"Technical or construction site issues accounted for only 25 per cent," he said in his speech at the Nexgen Builders Contractor 2026 Convention: Building a New Generation and launch of the Facility Management Good Practice Guide here today.
The guide, launched by the Construction Industry Development Board (CIDB), provides industry reference for systematic and sustainable facility management practices, in line with the National Construction Policy 2030.
Ahmad Maslan said contractors must take greater responsibility for ensuring projects were completed according to schedule, within budget and to the required standards.
He said a strong track record and project delivery capability should be among the key criteria for contractors seeking government tenders.
"Contractors must have the ability to complete projects according to schedule, within budget and to the required standards," he added.
Ahmad Maslan also urged contractors, particularly those in the lower grades, to strengthen their business capacity instead of remaining comfortable at their current level.
"Do not be comfortable remaining at G1. Upgrade your company systematically," he said.
He said contractors needed to modernise their operations through digital technology, including through the Building Information Modelling (BIM), to improve project delivery and remain competitive.
"Digital transformation is no longer an option," he said.
Ahmad Maslan said contractors also needed to improve their financial strength, management capabilities, quality and safety compliance, sustainability practices, integrity and strategic partnerships.
He said stronger governance and professional management were essential to reducing project delays and ensuring public development funds were used effectively.
Ahmad Maslan said the construction sector in Penang grew 13.4 per cent, while the state's overall economy expanded 7.3 per cent.

Title: Govt open to studying GST-SST combination for more progressive tax system
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: The government is open to studying a combination of the Goods and Services Tax (GST) and Sales and Services Tax (SST) as part of efforts to develop a more progressive tax system.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the government was prepared to review and improve the country's existing tax system, including considering certain features of GST that could be incorporated into the current SST framework.
"We are open to studying ways to improve the tax system. But if we are talking about GST alone, my concern, as I have said repeatedly, is that it would mean taxing the people.
"Although it is said to be more efficient, it is still a tax on the people. This means those who have never paid tax would also have to pay.
"How do we address that in the current situation, when people are already facing the cost of living and financial pressures?
"That is why we use SST as the basis, but if there are certain adjustments that can be made, we can consider them," he said when met by reporters here today.

Title: Too few facility management contractors despite RM39.59b opportunity
Article:
BUTTERWORTH: The limited number of facility management contractors represents a missed opportunity, with RM39.59 billion worth of projects recorded over three years.
Deputy Works Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Maslan said only 468 contractors were registered under the F01 and F02 facility management specialisations, despite 1,541 facility management and maintenance projects being recorded by the Construction Industry Development Board (CIDB) between 2023 and 2025.
He said the figures highlighted significant room for more contractors to enter the sector, particularly as the industry increasingly shifted towards managing and maintaining assets throughout their lifecycle.
"This is an opportunity that needs to be seized by contractors involved in facility management. We should not only be involved in construction, but also in maintenance," he told reporters after officiating the Nexgen Builders Contractor 2026 Convention: Building a New Generation and launching the Facility Management Good Practice Guide here today.
The guide, launched by CIDB, provides an industry reference for systematic and sustainable facility management practices in line with the National Construction Policy 2030.
Ahmad said facility management had previously received less attention because contractors and the industry traditionally focused on construction and regarded maintenance as a secondary activity.
"We did not have a maintenance mentality. We build, then leave it. We build, then leave it, whereas roads, bridges and buildings all require proper maintenance," he said.
He said proper maintenance could extend the lifespan of public assets while ensuring investments in infrastructure continued to deliver value to the people.
Ahmad said the RM39.59 billion value recorded for facility management and maintenance projects over the three-year period showed that the sector offered substantial business potential.
He urged more contractors to register with CIDB for facility management services and diversify beyond conventional construction activities.
"Hopefully, more contractors will register as facility management contractors so that the number can increase, even double, in the coming period," he said.
Ahmad said a larger pool of qualified contractors would also give asset owners and the Government more choices when appointing service providers.
He said the sector was no longer limited to building maintenance, but encompassed asset management, facility operations, technology, safety and sustainability.
He said contractors should view facility management as a way to diversify their businesses, develop new revenue streams and remain competitive as the construction industry evolves.

Title: Court directs Tun M to file Batu Puteh RCI report as fresh evidence
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: The Court of Appeal today directed Tun Dr Mahathir Mohamad to file an application to introduce the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) report on the Batu Puteh sovereignty issue as fresh evidence in his appeal.
The three-member panel comprising Datuk Azizul Azmi Adnan, Datuk Ong Chee Kwan and Datuk Seri Mohd Radzi Harun gave Dr Mahathir's lawyer, Zainur Zakaria, two weeks to file the application.
Earlier, Zainur told the court that the RCI report showed Dr Mahathir was the subject of the inquiry into the handling of the Batu Puteh issue.
He argued that Dr Mahathir had been denied the right to be present throughout the RCI proceedings and to challenge testimony against him.
The senior lawyer said a task force set up on Oct 8, 2021, as a precursor to the RCI, had concluded that Dr Mahathir was responsible for the loss of Batu Puteh.
Zainur said the RCI subsequently made findings implicating his client, including an allegation that Dr Mahathir had misled the Cabinet over the issue.
Azizul asked Zainur whether he was relying on the findings in the RCI's final report, to which the lawyer replied in the affirmative.
The judge then pointed out that Dr Mahathir's judicial review application had been filed before the RCI report was completed and that there had been no application previously to adduce the report as fresh evidence.
Azizul then directed Zainur to file the application and fixed Sept 10 for case management.
The appeal concerns Dr Mahathir's judicial review application seeking to allow him and his lawyer to be present throughout the RCI proceedings.
The High Court dismissed the application on Jan 13 last year, ruling that Dr Mahathir was not the subject matter of the RCI inquiry.
The RCI, which investigated the handling of Malaysia's sovereignty over Batu Puteh, Middle Rocks and South Ledge, heard testimony from Dr Mahathir on June 12, 2024.
Its report was declassified and made public on Dec 5, 2024.
Among its findings, the RCI concluded that Dr Mahathir may have deliberately encouraged the Cabinet not to pursue two legal applications to review and interpret the International Court of Justice's 2008 decision awarding sovereignty over Batu Puteh to Singapore.
The RCI also recommended that a criminal investigation be initiated against Dr Mahathir under Section 415(b) of the Penal Code, with possible punishment under Sections 417 and 418.
However, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said on July 22, 2025, that the government had decided not to proceed with action against Dr Mahathir over the Batu Puteh issue due to age-related considerations.
Dr Mahathir filed the judicial review application on June 5, 2024, naming eight respondents, including RCI chairman Tun Md Raus Sharif.
He is seeking a declaration that he was the subject of the RCI investigation or was involved in the matter being investigated, as well as a mandamus order compelling the commission to allow him and his lawyer to be present throughout its proceedings.

Title: Malaysia wary of BYD disrupting auto market as in Thailand – Ong Kian Ming
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The automotive industry is in a state of flux, as investments by Chinese automakers in Malaysia and Southeast Asia are disrupting their respective markets, causing governments to scramble to respond in order to protect their local players.
Taylor's University adjunct professor Dr Ong Kian Ming said while the impact of most Chinese carmakers' plans in Malaysia could be anticipated by the government, BYD Auto's plans are shifting the debate among ministers.
"BYD came in with certain proposals that I think were maybe anticipated by the Investment, Trade and Industry Ministry (Miti) but not anticipated by other members of the government. What do I mean by this?
"If you look at the completely knocked-down (CKD) proposals of all the other major Chinese players — Great Wall, Chery, of course, Geely via Proton — there was relatively good communication of those plans and the localisation plans with Miti," he said.
"For BYD, it was a bit different, because they had their experience in Thailand, where they went in with a big investment, 150,000 unit volume, a lot of that anticipated to sell into the domestic market which the total industry volume was about 700,000 units, smaller than Malaysia.
"That disrupted the auto sector there quite a bit, and of course Malaysia looked at that with great concern and said 'we don't want the same to happen to us'," the former deputy Miti minister said at the CGS International ESG and Sustainability Conference 2026.
Malaysia opened up its automotive market between 2022 and 2025 to imported completely built-up electric vehicles (EVs), which enticed automakers, especially from China, to enter the market with competitively priced products.
Meanwhile, locally assembled models are still allowed zero excise duty until 2027.
While BYD wanted to set up a local assembly plant in Tanjung Malim, Perak, the plan was put on hold after Investment, Trade and Industry Minister Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani announced that 80 per cent of the planned production volume must be exported.
GOVERNMENT COMMUNICATIONS LACKING IN EFFECTIVENESS
Ong also noted that the government's communication of its policies lacked effectiveness, causing public confusion and anger.
A case in point is the government's policy to restrict the sale of imported EVs to models with a cost, insurance and freight value of at least RM200,000, as well as batteries with a capacity of at least 180kilowatts.
The policy has been criticised by many as being aimed at protecting local automakers Proton Holdings Bhd and Perusahaan Otomobil Kedua Sdn Bhd (Perodua), as it makes most affordable EV models, especially those from China, ineligible for sale.
It was seen as the government trying to regress to the 1990s, when imported cars were expensive due to the national automotive aspiration at the time of growing Proton, and to a certain extent Perodua, into giant automotive groups.
Ong said that while it was true that the policy would protect Proton and Perodua, it would also protect the auto parts ecosystem in the country. However, this was not effectively communicated by Miti when it announced the restrictions.
"I think this is where the communications part is actually very important. I think in the larger discussion on the auto sector in Malaysia, we often forget that Malaysia is probably second in ASEAN with regards to our automotive parts ecosystem.
"So we actually export a lot more in terms of parts than the actual cars themselves. And because of the CKD policies that we've had over the years, this has actually increased the parts provision and also the manufacturing ecosystem in Malaysia.
"So much so that if you look at, for example, Vietnam, they're trying to produce their own car industry, they're trying to go into EVs, they can only probably produce 15 to 20 per cent of their parts. Whereas for Malaysia and Thailand, we can go up to 80 per cent," he said.
Ong added that when Miti announced these kinds of policies that affect consumers, there was no counter-narrative to explain how they would help local auto parts players, which have contributed significantly to the automotive industry.
POLICY ALIGNMENT AND UPDATE NEEDED
Ong also said the Malaysian government needs to update the National Automotive Policy to align it with current government policies.
He said if Malaysia wants to move towards an EV ecosystem, it needs to realign its policies with its approach to petrol subsidies.
He suggested there has to be consistency between the government's EV aspirations and its fuel subsidy programmes. Ideally, he said, the government should be able to reduce the subsidy quota or increase petrol prices slightly.
"My personal preference is actually to allow CKD competition below RM200,000 and not allow EVs priced at RM100,000 and below to be monopolised by one or two players," Ong said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Cabinet to table comprehensive plan to strengthen entry point controls tomorrow
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: A comprehensive plan to improve controls at the country's entry points will be tabled at the Cabinet meeting tomorrow, said Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail.
He said the plan would be jointly presented with Transport Minister Anthony Loke, as it included matters under the jurisdiction of the Transport Ministry.
He said the plan was prepared within two weeks following a Cabinet directive to strengthen controls at the country's entry points through greater coordination among relevant agencies.
"Tomorrow I will jointly present the comprehensive plan with my colleague, Anthony Loke, because it includes elements under the jurisdiction of the Transport Ministry," he said in his speech at the Home Ministry's monthly assembly here, today.
Earlier this month, the media reported that the Cabinet had instructed the Home Ministry and Transport Ministry to submit a comprehensive plan to improve security controls at Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) within two weeks.
The directive followed the Government's concerns over several recent incidents that could affect the country's image, as well as perceptions of weaknesses in the security control system at the airport.
Airport security controls came under scrutiny following several cases involving Malaysians, including the detention of a Malaysian pilot after about 25kg of MDMA was seized at Soekarno-Hatta International Airport in Indonesia recently.
Saifuddin said the plan would also take into account the need to improve coordination and cooperation between agencies to ensure more effective controls at the country's entry points.
He said areas being examined included improving human resource competencies, infrastructure requirements, closed-circuit television (CCTV) systems, scanning machines and training for personnel operating the equipment.
"We want to see which areas can be improved, whether in terms of infrastructure requirements, CCTV, scanning machines or training for those monitoring the scanning machines. We will look at everything," he said.
Saifuddin said the plan was drawn up by combining the knowledge, experience and expertise of various agencies under the Home Ministry, MOT and other relevant agencies.
He said the move was important to ensure any weaknesses at the country's entry points could be identified and addressed comprehensively, while preventing incidents that could affect the country's image from recurring.
On the investigation into the pilot's case, Saifuddin said the police had received good cooperation from the Indonesian authorities and had successfully interviewed the suspect for further action.
"The information we obtained will help us determine whether this is part of an international syndicate or an individual act, and so on.
"This gives us an opportunity to identify where the weaknesses or shortcomings are at our country's exit or entry points," he said.

Title: Consider random breathalyser tests for pilots, cabin crew
Article:
LETTERS:
THE recent incidents of pilots who tested positive for drug abuse should prompt airlines to raise their bar in regional screening to maintain public trust and aviation safety standards.
The recent two incidents in Asia have highlighted that human factors remain a critical vulnerability in safe aviation operations.
The first, on July 28 at Jakarta's Soekarno–Hatta International Airport, involved a co-pilot after a flight from Kuala Lumpur to Jakarta on a 737-800, who tested positive for methamphetamine.
He had about 26kg of ecstasy pills in his checked luggage, according to reports.
Then, in India, an airline pilot with the rank of captain on an Airbus A320 was involved in a serious mid-air incident on a flight from Phuket to Delhi.
He tested positive for marijuana after arrival on Aug 11.
It is of paramount importance that random checks be carried out before a flight by the authorities concerned.
Should the need arise, the reporting time for the operating crew can be extended for the test to be done.
The recent cases within two weeks may seem isolated. It, however, raises concern with regard to safety as pilots need to be fit and alert at all times during flight.
Therefore, random breathalyser tests should not be ruled out as a check.
As an example, a foreign airline Airbus A350 captain failed a random pre-flight alcohol breath test carried out by the local aviation authority in Melbourne on Sept 15, 2018.
He was immediately grounded. The captain was ordered by the airline to return to base as a passenger.
In that incident, more than 200 passengers on the international flight were stranded.
Nevertheless, the safety of the aircraft, crew and passengers is of paramount importance at all times of the flight.
Such checks should also be extended to cabin crew. They act as a safety tool to arrest abuse of prohibited substances to ensure safety for all.
WILLIAM DENNIS
Subang Jaya,
Selangor

Title: 1,500 cartons of duty-unpaid cigarettes found in bread consignment
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A 39-year-old Malaysian man was arrested in Singapore after allegedly attempting to smuggle 1,500 cartons of duty-unpaid cigarettes into the country in a Malaysia-registered lorry.
The Singapore Immigration and Checkpoints Authority said the contraband was uncovered after its officers flagged the vehicle for enhanced checks at the Tuas checkpoint on Aug 11.
"A total of 1500 cartons of duty-unpaid cigarettes were found concealed within a consignment of assorted bread.
"A 39-year-old male Malaysian was arrested in connection with the case," it said in a Facebook post today.
It said the exhibits and the suspect were referred to Singapore Customs for further investigation.

Title: More companies advertise jobs, but offerings fall 11.4pct in Q2
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The number of online job offerings advertised in Malaysia fell 11.4 per cent to 555,509 in the second quarter (Q2) of 2026 from 626,816 in the preceding quarter, the Statistics Department said.
Despite the decline, the number of companies advertising job openings rose marginally to 79,510 from 79,499 in the first quarter, according to the department's latest job market insights report.
Professionals accounted for the largest share of online job offerings at 51.5 per cent, or 285,907 positions, down 9.5 per cent from 315,768 in the previous quarter.
Managers followed with 87,950 job offerings, while technicians and associate professionals recorded 86,512.
Among individual occupations, advertising and marketing professionals were the most sought after, with 40,640 job offerings.
They were followed by managing directors and chief executives with 26,649 job offerings, administrative associate professionals with 23,984, accountants and auditors with 22,067, and software developers with 19,899.
The services sector continued to account for the largest share of online job offerings, with 243,896 positions, or 43.9 per cent of the total, in the second quarter.
Within the sector, the wholesale and retail trade; repair of motor vehicles and motorcycles subsector recorded the highest number of job offerings at 78,526.
This was followed by professional, scientific and technical activities with 32,127 offerings, administrative and support service activities with 28,788, accommodation and food service activities with 20,629, and financial and insurance/takaful activities with 20,593.
In the technical and vocational education and training field, technicians recorded the highest number of job offerings at 6,565, followed by engineers at 6,380 and sales managers at 4,957.
Similarly, in the science, technology, engineering and mathematics field, technicians topped the list with 6,565 job offerings, followed by engineers with 6,380 and account managers with 3,627.
Under the critical occupations list, assistant managers recorded the highest demand with 9,204 job offerings, followed by sales executives with 8,230 and account executives with 7,104.

Title: Bus Cap surges 80pct in three days, blows past analysts' fair values
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Shares of Bus Cap Bhd surged to a new high in active trade, extending a three-day advance of more than 80 per cent and pushing the newly listed bus manufacturer well past analysts' pre-listing fair values.
The stock jumped as much as nine sen, or 23.7 per cent, to a record high of 47 sen in the morning session, with more than 14 million shares traded. It opened 3.9 per cent, or 1.5 sen higher at 39.5 sen from Monday's close of 38 sen.
Over the three sessions, the counter has gained 80.77 per cent, or 21 sen, from last Thursday's close of 26 sen. It rose 25 per cent to 32.5 sen last Friday before climbing another 16.9 per cent to 38 sen on Monday.
The rally has also pushed Bus Cap's shares to more than double their initial public offering (IPO) price just over two months after its ACE Market debut on June 3.
At 47 sen, the company was valued at about RM180.19 million. Against its IPO price of 23 sen, the stock has gained 104.3 per cent and is 49.2 per cent higher than its first-day closing price of 31.5 sen.
Bus Cap currently has no analyst coverage, according to MyBursa.
Ahead of its listing, however, RHB Research had assigned the stock a fair value of 38 sen, implying a 66 per cent upside from its IPO price.
The firm had forecast Bus Cap's net profit to grow at a three-year compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of about 18 per cent from financial year 2025 (FY25) to FY28.
The growth was expected to be supported by rising bus demand from the tourism recovery, growing intercity and cross-border travel and recurring replacement demand.
Public Investment Bank Bhd (PublicInvest), meanwhile, had assigned a lower fair value of 28 sen, representing a 21.7 per cent potential return from the IPO price.
It had projected Bus Cap's earnings to grow at a three-year CAGR of about 15 per cent, underpinned by higher sales volumes, increasing average selling prices and production efficiency gains, as well as regulatory bus replacement cycles and growth in tourism and intercity travel.
At 47 sen, Bus Cap is trading 23.7 per cent above RHB Research's pre-listing fair value and 67.9 per cent above PublicInvest's.
Interest in the pureplay bus builder was strong even before its debut, with the public portion of its IPO oversubscribed by more than 72 times.
Ipoh-based Bus Cap, through its subsidiary Sin Hock Leong Coach Works Sdn Bhd, manufactures buses and coaches for local and overseas markets.

Title: Amir Hamzah: Tough economic reforms necessary despite unpopularity
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: Economic restructuring can be difficult, particularly when it involves unpopular policies, but such measures are necessary for long-term growth and the people's wellbeing, says Datuk Seri Amir Hamzah Azizan.
The Finance Minister II said reforms implemented by the government included electricity subsidy rationalisation from 2023, the expansion of the Sales and Services Tax (SST) and the phased implementation of the e-Invoicing system.
"Policies introduced are often unpopular, but they need to be implemented because they bring greater long-term benefits to the country and the people's well-being," he said in his speech at the 2027 Budget Engagement Session at the Finance Ministry here today.
Amir Hamzah said the phased implementation of electricity subsidy rationalisation had not affected the majority of Malaysians, with 85 per cent of domestic users remaining protected.
He said the measure had also supported the sustainability of the country's energy sector, while the expansion of the SST had contributed positively to revenue consolidation without undermining domestic purchasing power through a progressive approach based on social justice.
"The phased implementation of e-invoicing has now become a cornerstone of efforts to improve transparency in the country's business ecosystem.
"The system is not intended to be burdensome, but instead helps reduce the size of the shadow economy, improve tax assessment efficiency and accelerate domestic tax governance," he said.
Amir Hamzah said Malaysia's economy remained on a strong footing, with gross domestic product (GDP) growing 5.4 per cent in the first quarter of 2026 and six per cent in the second quarter, bringing first-half growth to 5.7 per cent.
He said the performance exceeded Bank Negara Malaysia's (BNM) 2026 GDP growth forecast of between four and five per cent, reflecting the resilience of the Malaysian economy amid global uncertainty.
The International Monetary Fund (IMF) also raised its forecast for Malaysia's GDP growth from 4.3 per cent in January 2026 to 4.7 per cent in April, maintaining the forecast in its latest publication in July, while the ringgit remained stable during the first seven months of the year.
"Approved investments in 2025 reached a record RM431.1 billion, an 11 per cent increase, while approved investments in the first quarter of 2026 remained strong at RM92.8 billion," he said.
However, he said, economic achievements would mean little if Malaysians continued to struggle with the cost of living.
He said although inflation for the first seven months of the year rose to 1.8 per cent following an increase in global crude oil prices amid the conflict in West Asia, the government continued to take measures to ease the burden on the people.
"Among them, allocations for Sumbangan Tunai Rahmah (STR) and Sumbangan Asas Rahmah (Sara) were increased from RM10 billion in 2024 to RM15 billion, making it the largest targeted assistance allocation in history.
"The government has also expanded the Madani Rahmah Sales Programme, offering goods at between 10 and 30 per cent below market prices across all 600 state constituencies and all 40 zones in the Federal Territories of Putrajaya, Kuala Lumpur and Labuan, with 15,881 programmes held as of June 30.
"In addition, targeted diesel subsidies through the Budi Madani Diesel mechanism were implemented from July 1, allowing eligible Malaysians to purchase subsidised diesel at RM2.10 a litre, with a basic monthly limit of up to 200 litres," he said.

Title: Bond yields jump, oil extends gains as US-Iran ceasefire expires
Article:
SINGAPORE: Bond yields climbed on Tuesday to their highest in decades, with oil prices rising for a third day, while stocks gave up early gains in Asian trade as a US-Iran truce expired and Tehran threatened to adopt a "fully offensive" military posture.
The yield on the US 30-year Treasury bond rose as much as 1.1 basis points to an intraday high of 5.321 per cent, its highest in almost 20 years. Its 10-year counterpart traded up 0.4 basis point at 4.724 per cent.
"Typically, moves above 4.65 per cent for the US 10-year have been followed by some soothing words from the Trump administration, typically centred on an imminent resolution to the war with Iran," ING analysts wrote in a note.
"This time, we're not hearing the same," they added. "In fact, the latest indications are for no imminent resolution as the shaky 60-day truce came to an end."
S&P 500 e-mini futures slumped 0.2 per cent as MSCI's broadest index of Asia-Pacific shares outside Japan slid 0.3 per cent, reversing early gains as stocks in Taiwan and China weighed on the benchmark.
South Korea's KOSPI erased an early gain of more than 3 per cent as the Seoul market returned after a holiday to trade flat, while the Nikkei 225 fell 1.6 per cent.
Brent crude futures edged up 0.4 per cent to US$91.20 a barrel as a rally in oil prices extended into a third consecutive day in Asian trade.
"The big focus in global macro is the increase and stickiness in longer-end developed market yields, and in particular a relentless sell-off in US Treasuries," MUFG analysts wrote in a research report.
As the recent global selloff in bonds deepened, the yield on the 10-year Japanese government bond rose 2 basis points to 2.94 per cent, a three-decade high.
Overnight on Wall Street, the S&P 500 slipped 0.5 per cent while the Nasdaq Composite edged 0.3 per cent lower as soft US economic data, including an unexpected drop in retail sales, led traders to reduce bets on an imminent Fed interest rate move.
"Markets adopted a generally risk-off tone as President Trump reaffirmed he was not interested in extending the truce with Iran," Westpac analysts wrote in a research note.
The US dollar index, a measures of the greenback's strength against a basket of six currencies, was up 0.1 per cent at 99.60, pulling back from a two-month low.
Gold was down 0.3 per cent at US$4,402.89, snapping a two-day winning streak.
In cryptocurrencies, bitcoin and ether were both down 0.3 per cent at US$64,159.76 and US$1,899.34 respectively.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Temerloh crash: Fuel tanker driver claims trial over mother, son's deaths
Article:
TEMERLOH: A fuel tanker driver claimed trial at the magistrate's court here today to two counts of dangerous driving that resulted in the deaths of a mother and her son at Km9 of Jalan Temerloh-Triang last week.
Nor Azlan Mahayudin, 37, pleaded not guilty after the charges were read separately to him before magistrate Anis Adlina Abu Johan.
The accused, who was driving the tanker, was charged with dangerous driving that resulted in the death of 39-year-old Nur Fatimah Syuhada Abdullah.
He was alleged to have committed the offence at Km9 of Jalan Temerloh-Triang at about 4pm on Aug 14.
On the second charge, Nor Azlan was charged with dangerous driving that resulted in the death of Muhamad Fattah Aisy Nuafal Saifulnizam, 12, at the same location and time.
The charges were framed under Section 41(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987 for causing death by reckless or dangerous driving, which carries a maximum jail term of 10 years and a fine of up to RM50,000 upon conviction.
Deputy public prosecutor Amal Razim Alias appeared for the prosecution, while Nor Azlan was represented by Mazieera Sharifudin from the National Legal Aid Foundation (YBGK).
Anis Adlina set bail at RM10,000 with one surety and fixed Oct 1 for mention.
In the incident, Nur Fatimah Syuhada and Fattah Aisy were burnt to death after their car was crushed by the tanker, which was carrying 32,000 litres of diesel and petrol.
The crash caused both vehicles to catch fire, trapping the victims inside. They were buried yesterday.

Title: [UPDATED] Fire Skills Hub to strengthen first response before firefighters arrive
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Building operators are being trained to become the Fire and Rescue Department's "eyes, ears, hands and feet" during emergencies under a nationwide programme to strengthen fire safety at premises.
Fire and Rescue Department director-general Datuk Seri Nor Hisham Mohammad said the Fire Skills Hub was designed to equip personnel at designated premises with practical skills to respond before firefighters arrive.
He said the initiative, developed in collaboration with HRD Corp, would support the appointment and development of fire safety managers and fire safety officers at premises gazetted under fire certification requirements.
"Part of the requirement for their appointment is that they attend the Fire Skills Hub.
"This will then be followed by specific courses for fire safety officers and fire safety managers, followed by an assessment by the Department of Skills Development," he said after launching the Fire Skills Hub for Kuala Lumpur, Putrajaya and Negri Sembilan.
Nor Hisham said the eventual goal was for participants to obtain competency recognition through the Malaysian Skills Certificate Level Three within three years.
Unlike conventional fire safety programmes centred mainly on briefings and lectures, he said participants would receive hands-on exposure to firefighting equipment, building safety systems and emergency procedures.
Nor Hisham described participants as a "force multiplier" rather than replacements for firefighters, allowing trained personnel to take appropriate action during emergencies at their respective premises.
He said such capability was important as the department could not realistically inspect every premise in the country.
He acknowledged that the sheer number of premises compared with the department's capacity made 100 per cent inspection impossible, requiring inspections to instead be focused, risk-based and conducted according to identified priorities.
This, he said, made self-regulation by building owners and operators an important first line of defence against major fires.
"Two earlier series involving participants from Sabah, Labuan, Selangor and Perak drew 2,395 people, while more than 1,500 participants from Kuala Lumpur, Putrajaya and Negri Sembilan attended today's programme.
"The programme will subsequently be taken to Johor, Terengganu, Penang and Sarawak," he said.
Nor Hisham said the collaboration with HRD Corp would also allow eligible industries to utilise training funds from levies they had paid, reducing the direct financial burden on businesses participating in the programme.

Title: [UPDATED] Fire and Rescue Dept monitoring 62 locations at risk of major fires
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Fire and Rescue Department is closely monitoring 62 locations nationwide at risk of large-scale fires covering more than 25ha amid a sharp rise in open fires this year.
Its director-general Datuk Seri Nor Hisham Mohammad said the locations were among 183 hotspots identified nationwide as being prone to open fires based on records from the past five years.
"We specifically monitor 183 locations nationwide which we have identified as areas exposed to open fires based on records over the past five years.
"From that, we have 62 locations which we have identified as prone to large fires of more than 25ha," he said after launching the Fire Skills Hub for Kuala Lumpur, Putrajaya and Negri Sembilan today.
Nor Hisham said the 62 locations were receiving particular attention because fires there could spread rapidly and require substantial mobilisation of firefighting resources.
He said the department's objective was to prevent fires from repeatedly occurring at the same locations and, should a blaze break out, stop it from spreading rapidly.
"The heightened monitoring comes as the department recorded 18,432 forest, bush and rubbish fire incidents between January and July this year.
"This compares with 9,941 incidents during the corresponding period last year and 16,294 in 2024," he said.
Nor Hisham said the figures showed a sharp increase from last year, with numerous smaller fires reported across the peninsula, while larger incidents were recorded in Sarawak.
"Among the major fires currently of concern were incidents in Sri Aman and Mukah.
"Sabah was also receiving particular attention because of vegetation such as acacia and bertam, which could contribute to rapidly spreading fires," he said adding that seven major fire locations around Kota Kinabalu were recorded in 2024 and had been included among the 62 locations now under close watch.
"The fire spreads quickly there and is also difficult to control because it involves hilly areas," he said.
He said no quick response teams had been specifically deployed to the identified hotspots for now as there were currently no widespread major fires requiring such mobilisation.
However, the department was already preparing for the possible impact of a strong El Niño, including strengthening coordination with other agencies.
Nor Hisham said while the phenomenon was expected to develop in the Pacific around November, its effects on Malaysia could begin to be felt as early as the third or fourth week of January next year.
He said particular attention would be given to the northern peninsula, east coast and Sabah, although fire risks remained in other areas.
Nor Hisham also urged the public to refrain from open burning, particularly as haze was already affecting air quality.
"People are already having a difficult time, the haze has started coming in and it is getting harder to breathe. Don't burn," he said.

Title: [UPDATED] Fire and Rescue Dept mulls home EV charging guidelines after Cheras blaze
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Fire and Rescue Department may introduce safety guidelines for electric vehicle (EV) charging at private homes following Sunday's fire at a house in Cheras.
Its director-general Datuk Seri Nor Hisham Mohammad said there were currently no specific guidelines governing EV charging installations at private homes.
He said the current guidelines only focused on commercial premises.
"We will raise this issue with the relevant authorities. For homes, we don't have one yet. Our controls at the moment are for commercial premises," he said after launching the Fire Skills Hub for Kuala Lumpur, Putrajaya and Negri Sembilan today.
However, Nor Hisham said investigators had yet to conclude that the EV itself caused the Aug 16 fire in Cheras.
He said witness accounts, including information from the house owner, had led investigators to consider several possible causes involving the EV charging system.
"These included the vehicle itself, its charging equipment or the electrical wiring connected to the charger.
"We cannot conclude yet. We have to wait for the investigation to be completed," he said.
Nor Hisham said statistics recorded about 25 fire cases involving four categories of EVs over the past three years.
The number, he said, had remained relatively stable each year rather than showing a significant increase.
However, he acknowledged that the number of EVs on Malaysian roads was also growing, while the department had yet to analyse fire incidents against the increase in the EV population.
Nor Hisham advised homeowners using EV chargers to ensure the equipment complied with recognised safety standards, particularly if the chargers were purchased separately rather than supplied as part of a vehicle package.
He said installation should also be carried out by registered and qualified companies, with the home's electrical wiring properly inspected before the charger was installed.
"Particular attention should be paid to the size and suitability of electrical wiring as well as the miniature circuit breaker (MCB) system.
"This was important because EVs could be continuously charged for seven to eight hours, creating an electrical fire risk if the installation or wiring was unsuitable," he said.
Nor Hisham said lessons from a previous fire involving a private charging bay had pointed to the electrical wiring connected to the system rather than the charger itself.
He said the department would examine the findings of the Cheras investigation before engaging industry players on whether
further measures
were needed.
It was reported that an EV being charged at the foyer of a double-storey terrace house was believed to have sparked a fire that destroyed the property in Alam Damai, Cheras, on Sunday.
The Kuala Lumpur Fire and Rescue Department said it received an emergency call via NG999 at 5.03am about the fire at a house near Surau At Taqwa in Jalan Murni 10.
Firefighters found the 20ft by 60ft double-storey terrace house engulfed in flames upon arrival.
The property was completely destroyed, but no casualties were reported. The operation ended at 6.41am.

Title: Philippine student killed in school shooting
Article:

Title: 2027 Budget to ease cost of living, boost economic resilience
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: The 2027 Budget will prioritise easing cost-of-living pressures, strengthening social protection and improving education, healthcare and basic services while boosting Malaysia's economic competitiveness and resilience.
Finance Minister II Datuk Seri Amir Hamzah Azizan said the fifth Madani Budget, which is set to be tabled on Oct 9, would focus on three broad priorities.
This includes raising the economic ceiling, raising the social floor and strengthening good governance.
Amir Hamzah said the government would also prioritise food security, business productivity and fiscal sustainability.
"Under efforts to raise the ceiling, the government will prioritise high-value investment, productivity and strategic sectors, including semiconductors, energy transition, the digital economy, artificial intelligence and Islamic finance.
"Small and medium enterprises and start-ups will also receive greater support through financing, digitalisation, innovation and market expansion," he said during his keynote address at the 2027 Budget Engagement Session here today.
On 'raising the floor', Amir said attention would remain on education, healthcare, human capital development, quality employment, household incomes and stronger social protection for vulnerable groups.
"The government will also continue efforts to improve regulations, facilitate investment, digitise public services and reduce bureaucracy as part of its good governance agenda," he said.
Amir Hamzah said the government had identified 10 priority areas in its Pre-Budget Statement to guide consultations before the budget is finalised.
He said the budget would seek to ensure that economic growth translated into more inclusive benefits for Malaysians while strengthening the country's ability to withstand external shocks.
"Although the country's achievements are encouraging, they become meaningless if the people are still struggling with the cost of living," he said.
He said the government would also continue targeted assistance, including increasing allocations for Sumbangan Tunai Rahmah (STR) and Sumbangan Asas Rahmah (Sara) from RM10 billion in 2024 to RM15 billion.
The allocation, he said, included Sara Appreciation aid payouts for 22 million Malaysians aged 18 and above to help sustain domestic purchasing power.
"The government will also continue the Madani Rahmah Sales programme, which offers selected goods at 10 to 30 per cent below market prices, as well as targeted diesel subsidies under Budi Madani Diesel," he said.
He said eligible Malaysians would continue to receive subsidised diesel at RM2.10 a litre, with a basic monthly limit of 200 litres.
"Meanwhile, the Budi Madani RON95 programme would maintain the subsidised RON95 price at RM1.99 a litre for eligible Malaysians, subject to a monthly usage limit of 200 litres," he said.
On economic performance, Amir Hamzah said Malaysia's gross domestic product (GDP) grew 5.4 per cent in the first quarter of 2026 and 6 per cent in the second quarter, bringing first-half growth to 5.7 per cent.
He said the performance exceeded Bank Negara Malaysia's 2026 growth forecast of between four and five per cent.
"Approved investments reached a record RM431.1 billion last year, an 11 per cent increase, while approved investments in the first quarter of 2026 remained strong at RM92.8 billion.
"Malaysia also climbed eight places to 15th in the 2026 World Competitiveness Index, while Moody's Ratings maintained the country's A3 credit rating with a stable outlook," he said.
He said the government would continue fiscal reforms, including broadening the revenue base, optimising spending and improving targeted subsidy mechanisms.
He explained that the expansion of the Sales and Services Tax (SST), phased implementation of e-invoicing and electricity subsidy rationalisation were among measures aimed at strengthening public finances without undermining domestic purchasing power.
Amir Hamzah also called on the public and stakeholders to submit their proposals through the Finance Ministry's 2027 Budget Suggestions Portal.
Almost 400 representatives from the public and private sectors, business chambers, economists, academics, non-governmental organisations and international organisations attended today's engagement session.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Crude extends gains, stocks stagger as Mideast hopes dim
Article:
HONG KONG: Oil prices extended gains and stocks stuttered Tuesday as a US-Iran deal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz remained distant, a day after the deadline for a truce between the foes expired.
While soft US data this month has eased concerns that the Federal Reserve will hike interest rates soon, traders still expect inflation to remain high for some time as the Middle East crisis continues and crude stays stuck around $90 a barrel.
That has pushed up long-term Treasury yields to levels not seen since June 2007 -- just before the global financial crisis exploded -- compounded by rising US borrowing and massive corporate bond issuance to fund AI investments.
The chances of an agreement between Washington and Tehran remain thin after Donald Trump said he would not extend a 60-day truce -- part of a June memorandum of understanding -- and Iran called it "irrelevant" because the US had violated it early on.
The US president's envoy and son-in-law Jared Kushner said the two sides were having "very positive and active conversations" but noted that "there's really not a lot of trust between America and Iran after all these years".
"President Trump is going to be very patient... he doesn't want to rush to a deal," he told Fox News.
"He'll make the right deal when the right deal is ready," he added.
Earlier, Trump said Iranian officials "want to make a deal, but they're not going to make the kind of a deal that I feel is necessary".
He also threatened to bomb Oman if it "gets in the way" of an agreement, referring to ongoing talks between Muscat and Tehran on control of the waterway.
Washington appears happy to play a long game, which investors fear could mean prices will stay higher for some time.
Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent threatened last week to hit Tehran with economic isolation "like the world has never seen before", adding that new measures were expected next week.
That came after Trump had said "we are low-keying it", adding that "we are just watching Iran with its huge inflation and the fact they have no money".
Both main crude contracts rose Tuesday, following gains of more than two per cent the previous day, with Brent sitting above $91.
Equities were mixed.
Seoul rallied more than two per cent in early trade as it reopened after a long weekend, but pared the gains, while Sydney, Wellington and Jakarta also rose.
However, Tokyo, Hong Kong, Shanghai, Singapore, Taipei and Manila were all down.
"For weeks, investors had been willing to treat the Iran war, oil volatility and the pressure building in the long end of the Treasury curve as separate irritants," said Stephen Innes, global strategist at Quintex Intel.
"Diplomacy was supposed to contain the geopolitical risk, oil was supposed to remain manageable, and strong earnings were supposed to keep the equity engine turning.
"That calculus becomes less comfortable once those risks begin to converge."
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Dollar feeble as rate hike bets dwindle, Iran war worries grow
Article:
SINGAPORE: The US dollar held near multi-month lows against most major currencies on Tuesday as traders walked back expectations of near-term monetary tightening, although the imminent threat of an escalation in the Middle East war left sentiment fragile.
The euro fetched US$1.1581 in early Asian hours, not far from the two-month high of US$1.1614 it touched on Monday. Sterling was at US$1.3548, just shy of the three-month peak it touched in the previous session.
Data showed last week that US retail sales fell in July for the first time in nine months, following unexpected job losses last month and mild inflation readings. The run of softer data has led investors to scale back expectations of a rate hike by the US Federal Reserve.
Traders expect a 35 per cent chance of a rate increase at the Fed's September meeting, compared with 52.2 per cent a week ago, according to the CME FedWatch tool.
Analysts though remain cautious of where inflation may head, especially with the critical Strait of Hormuz remaining effectively shut and an impasse in the talks to end the US-Iran conflict.
"Inflation has been above target for most of the past five years, and whilst a high 2 per cent annual pace may prove acceptable to the Fed, it leaves the inflation process with little to no breathing room in a world of constant supply shocks," said Nohshad Shah, head of EMEA fixed income sales at Citadel Securities.
Iran said it would shift to a "fully offensive" military posture because efforts to negotiate a permanent end to the war with the US have stalled, a senior Iranian official told Reuters as Washington ruled out extending their June ceasefire agreement.
Bond yields around the world were on the rise again as traders remained wary of the impact of elevated oil prices and a prolonged closure of the Strait of Hormuz.
Brent crude futures were 0.3 per cent higher at US$91.14 a barrel after rising to their highest since July 30 on Monday.
The yield on the 30-year bond hovered near its highest level in nearly 20 years, while the 10-year JGB yield hit its highest level since September 1996.
The spotlight has also been on recent US Treasury auctions in the past week for the multi-decade yields demanded by investors to absorb Washington's borrowing needs.
"When it comes to longer-dated Treasury issuance, investors are increasingly focused and concerned about the growing amount of US debt and America's lack of fiscal discipline," said Anthony Saglimbene, chief market strategist at Ameriprise Financial.
"Frequent, large-scale treasury auctions are a chance for the bond market to push back against the government's eroding fiscal trajectory, as they demand higher yields for the auctions to clear."
The yen was stuck just below the 160 level, shifting the focus to the Bank of Japan meeting next month, where the central bank is set to raise interest rates and is considering hiking more aggressively after that, sources told Reuters.
It was last at 159.46 per US dollar, having erased nearly half of the gains from the joint US and Japan intervention at the end of July to lift the fragile yen away from 40-year lows.
The Australian dollar firmed 0.11 per cent to US$0.71119, perched near its strongest level since early June. The New Zealand dollar was at US$0.5902.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Education DG: SPM schedule to be announced today [WATCH]
Article:
KOTA BARU: The 2026 Sijil Pelajaran Malaysia (SPM) examination schedule is expected to be announced this evening after receiving the approval of Education Minister Fadhlina Sidek, said Education director-general Datuk Dr Mohd Azam Ahmad.
He said the proposed improvement to the examination schedule would be presented by the deputy director of the Examination Syndicate to Fadhlina today for consideration and approval.
"If there are no issues, we will release (the 2026 SPM schedule) this evening as well," he told reporters after the handover of a bus at Sekolah Menengah Kebangsaan Agama Naim Lilbanat, here, today.
He said the preparation of the new schedule took into account the views of various parties, including concerns regarding the status of several examination papers which were previously often scheduled at the end of the examination period.
"When we take all the views, we want to make some improvements to the SPM examination schedule, but we have to take time to discuss with the parties involved," he said.
He said other factors that were also being studied were the Northeast Monsoon, the haze incident that could occur at the end of the year and the school holiday period, to ensure that the set schedule did not have implications for the State Education Department (JPN), District Education Office (PPD) and schools.
"We are studying everything, that's why when we want to make changes, I want this (SPM 2026 Schedule) to be studied thoroughly," he said.
He said it was important so that any changes to the examination schedule would take into account the situation at the state and school levels as well as the interests of candidates and parents.
"We at the Ministry of Education will try to provide the best for the JPN, PPD and schools, especially our children who will be sitting for the SPM examination and also for parents," he said.
Meanwhile, when asked whether the Northeast Monsoon factor on the East Coast was among the main considerations, he said that the matter was indeed taken into account along with other weather factors such as the haze that occurs at uncertain times.
Mohd Azam said he had informed the minister of the proposal in a meeting yesterday and provided an initial overview of the proposed changes.
Recently, concerns from parents and candidates regarding the 2026 SPM examination date and schedule have gone viral on social media, with some questioning the delay in announcing the schedule. — BERNAMA
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Gold extends gains on easing rate-hike fears, markets await Fed minutes
Article:
NEW YORK: Gold rose for a third straight session on Tuesday as fears of a US interest rate hike next month eased, with investors awaiting minutes from the Federal Reserve's latest meeting for fresh clues on the monetary policy path.
Spot gold was up 0.2 per cent at US$4,424.28 per ounce by 0130 GMT, while US gold futures for December delivery edged 0.2 per cent higher to US$4,480.90.
The US dollar lingered around multi-month lows against most major currencies. A weaker US currency makes dollar-priced metals less expensive for holders of other currencies.
Gold is extending its gains "after last week's soft US economic data, which has raised hopes that the Fed will keep rates on hold this year," IG market analyst Tony Sycamore said.
Bullion tends to perform well in a low-interest-rate environment as it reduces the opportunity cost of holding non-yielding assets.
The US central bank will keep its key interest rate unchanged next month and through year-end, according to most economists in a Reuters poll.
Market pricing for a September quarter-point hike flipped to a near-65 per cent chance of a hold after unexpected job losses in July, lower-than-expected consumer price inflation and weaker retail sales.
Market focus will be on the minutes of the Fed's most recent policy meeting, due to be released on Wednesday.
"Additionally, gold appears to be regaining its safe-haven status as hawkish rhetoric from Iran helped gold brush off higher yields," Sycamore said.
Iran will shift to a "fully offensive" military posture because efforts to negotiate a permanent end to the war with the US have stalled, a senior Iranian official told Reuters, as Washington ruled out extending a temporary ceasefire agreement.
Among other metals, spot silver rose 0.9 per cent to US$66.40 per ounce. Platinum inched 0.2 per cent higher to US$1,772.75, while palladium was down 0.3 per cent at US$1,330.05.

Title: Japan's Nikkei slides as Middle East stalemate fuels oil, inflation concerns
Article:
TOKYO: Japan's Nikkei share average fell on Tuesday, putting it on course to snap a five-day winning streak, as a stalemate in the Middle East conflict drove oil prices higher and renewed concerns about bond market risks and inflation.
The Nikkei dropped 1.1 per cent to 68,460.56 by late morning, after a 5.5 per cent gain over the previous five trading sessions.
The broader Topix eased 0.2 per cent to 4,177.50.
A truce between the US and Iran expired this week, with Washington ruling out extending a ceasefire and Tehran saying it would shift to a "fully offensive" military posture.
Crude oil climbed as traffic through the crucial Strait of Hormuz shipping corridor again ground to a halt, and concerns about global inflation saw bond yields jump, including in Japan.
"Rising interest rates tend to highlight the relative overvaluation of share prices," said Wataru Akiyama, an equities strategist at Nomura Securities.
"Underlying concerns regarding persistently high inflation — which are present in both Japan and the US — could well act as a drag on the stock market going forward."
At the same time, shipping stocks benefited from expectations for higher freight rates, and marine transport was the best performer among the Tokyo Stock Exchange's 33 industry groupings, rallying 4.1 per cent.
AI stocks were split, with startup investor SoftBank Group rising 2.7 per cent, while chip-testing equipment manufacturer Tokyo Electron dived 4.3 per cent.

Title: US Navy destroyer left without power for four days in South China Sea
Article:
WASHINGTON: The USS Benfold, an Arleigh Burke-class guided-missile destroyer, was left without power for four days in the South China Sea last month following an engineering failure, Anadolu Ajansi reported.
"On July 24, 2026, while conducting routine operations in the Indo-Pacific, Arleigh Burke-class guided-missile destroyer USS Benfold (DDG 65) reported an engineering casualty involving its generators, causing a loss of power," Cmdr Matthew Comer, a spokesperson for the US 7th Fleet, told USNI News in a statement.
"There were no injuries to the crew, who demonstrated resilience, grit, professionalism and unwavering steadiness in their response," Comer said.
According to the statement, the power outage left the sailors without galley services, functioning toilets or air conditioning and affected the ship's potable water supply.
Comer said the George Washington Carrier Strike Group, with which the Benfold had been sailing, supported the destroyer during the incident.
The USS Robert Smalls, a cruiser attached to the strike group, helped provide meals for the crew.
An investigation into the cause of the incident is ongoing.

Title: TH welcomes move to amend Act, committed to strengthening governance
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Tabung Haji (TH) Board welcomes the government's move to amend the Tabung Haji Act 1995, in line with the recommendations of the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI).
The amendments, TH said, would help strengthen governance and ensure the responsibilities entrusted to TH continue to be upheld.
It said as an Islamic financial institution managing Muslims' savings for the purpose of performing the haj, it was committed to strengthening governance, transparency and integrity to safeguard depositors' interests and the institution's sustainability.
"TH will continue to support every improvement effort to strengthen the trust of depositors and ensure that this trust continues to be preserved for future generations," it said in a post on TH's official Facebook yesterday.
On Sunday, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, in a post on Facebook, said the government would implement amendments to the TH Act 1995 to ensure that the trust of Muslims continues to be preserved.

Title: SkyeChip's AI expansion to yield meaningful earnings from 2029
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: SkyeChip Bhd's expansion into artificial intelligence (AI) silicon and Arm-based compute platforms is expected to contribute limited revenue in the near term, UOB Kay Hian (M) Sdn Bhd said.
The firm said more meaningful earnings contributions are likely to emerge only after successful tape-out and volume production.
UOB Kay Hian said the initiatives could provide a second leg of growth for the semiconductor company from 2029 onwards.
"In the meantime, SkyeChip's established silicon intellectual property (IP) and custom application-specific integrated circuit (Asic) businesses should remain the key earnings drivers," it said in a note.
The firm said SkyeChip's recent engagement with Cerebras Systems for custom interface IP demonstrated the company's ability to participate in advanced AI computing platforms.
SkyeChip has also entered into a definitive agreement with the Malaysian Investment Development Authority for access to Arm's Flexible Access token, giving it access to Arm's comprehensive IP portfolio through an asset-light model.
The company is also targeting the finalisation of its Arm Compute Subsystems definitive agreement by financial year 2027 (FY27).
"These initiatives support its expansion into custom compute and AI hardware accelerators, including purpose-built Asics for specialised workloads such as tensor processing and data preprocessing, and high-performance central processing units and AI platforms for server and edge applications," it said.
UOB Kay Hian has raised its FY27 to FY29 earnings forecasts by two per cent following housekeeping adjustments.
Meanwhile, Hong Leong Investment Bank Bhd (HLIB) said SkyeChip's quarterly earnings are likely to remain lumpy due to its milestone-based revenue recognition.
By segment, silicon IP contributed RM26.3 million, or 53 per cent of total revenue, while custom Asic revenue stood at RM23.3 million, accounting for 47 per cent.
Custom Asic revenue has strengthened over the past two quarters, supported by an RM78 million unbilled order book as at end-March 2026.
"Of this, RM48 million is expected to be recognised in FY27, with the remaining RM30 million spread across FY28-FY29," HLIB said.
By geography, the US emerged as SkyeChip's largest market in the first quarter of FY27, contributing RM27.1 million, or 55 per cent of revenue, ahead of China at RM20.9 million, or 42 per cent.
"While we do not expect this mix to be sustained for the full year, the scale of the step-up in US revenue is significant and underscores SkyeChip's efforts to diversify away from its China and Taiwan exposure," it said.
UOB Kay Hian downgraded SkyeChip to "Hold" with a rolled-over target price of RM2.93 from RM2.08, while HLIB maintained its "Hold" call with an unchanged target price of RM2.95.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 99 Speed Mart poised for stronger second half
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: 99 Speed Mart Retail Holdings Bhd is expected to deliver stronger earnings in the second half of financial year 2026 (FY26), supported by seasonal spending and continued store expansion.
CIMB Securities Sdn Bhd analyst Walter Aw Lik Hsin said resilient demand for essential goods should also support the convenience store operator's earnings despite cautious consumer sentiment.
He said earnings could remain softer in the third quarter (Q3) of FY26 in the absence of major festive periods.
However, he expects performance to improve in Q4 FY26, driven by year-end festive spending, continued store expansion and resilient demand for essential goods.
"Despite softer consumer spending, we believe 99 Speed Mart's essentials-heavy and value-oriented positioning should support resilient demand, with additional benefits from consumer downtrading and higher in-home consumption," he said in a research note.
Aw said the company should also continue to benefit from government cash-aid programmes, with about 3,000 outlets, or 95.2 per cent of its total outlet base as at end-Q2, participating in the Sumbangan Asas Rahmah (Sara) programme.
However, he expects the incremental uplift from Sara to moderate as the programme matures and participation broadens across more retailers and eligible products.
The number of participating outlets nationwide rose to about 13,700 in July 2026, more than tripling from about 4,100 a year earlier, he said.
CIMB Securities maintained its "Hold" call on 99 Speed Mart while raising its target price to RM3.50 from RM3.40, based on a higher 2027 price-to-earnings (P/E) multiple of 37 times.
Aw said the company's defensive earnings profile and Sara-related tailwinds were largely reflected in its current valuation, which stood at about 38.5 times 2027 P/E.
"While we continue to favour 99 Speed Mart for its resilient business model, extensive distribution network and strong execution track record, we take a more cautious stance given the limited room for earnings disappointment at current valuations," he said.
99 Speed Mart recorded a net profit of RM163.95 million in Q2 FY26, up 13.4 per cent from RM144.63 million a year earlier.
The higher profit was driven by the continued expansion of its outlet network and the nationwide implementation of earlier opening hours, which supported higher customer traffic.
Revenue rose 13.6 per cent to RM3.1 billion from RM2.7 billion a year earlier.
For the first half of FY26, net profit surged 21.8 per cent to RM352.5 million from RM289.5 million, while revenue grew 15.5 per cent to RM6.14 billion from RM5.3 billion.
Hong Leong Investment Bank Bhd analyst Jonathan Ooi said the company's outlook remained constructive, underpinned by its defensive consumer staples business, 3,151-store network and ongoing structural cost efficiencies.
The commissioning of a new distribution centre in Semenyih in July is also expected to improve supply chain efficiency for about 180 surrounding outlets.
He said revenue should benefit further from an enhanced product mix following the nationwide rollout of home appliances across physical stores and 99 Bulksales, as well as new instalment plans aimed at improving affordability.
"While macro headwinds like cost of living pressures and cautious consumer spending persist, we expect margins to remain insulated, buffered by its ongoing energy-efficiency initiatives," Ooi said.
HLIB kept its "Buy" call on 99 Speed Mart and RM4.24 target price.
RHB Research analyst Soong Wei Siang also maintained a "Buy" call with a RM4.02 target price.
Soong said first-half results were in line with expectations, supported by robust sales momentum and effective cost control.
"99 Speed Mart's steady sales volume trend should be sustained, in view of its staples-oriented product mix and highly accessible outlet locations.
"It is also well-positioned to continue capitalising on the Sara programme, with about 3,000 outlets enrolled as panel stores," he said.
Management is also looking to add fewer than 10 outlets in China, with the overseas venture still at an experimental stage.
Beyond the near term, Soong said earnings growth could be supported by the company's efforts to expand its addressable market through diversified sourcing, electrical appliance sales, its bulk sales platform and overseas expansion.
He said sentiment towards the stock could also improve if the 2027 Budget provides a higher allocation for Sara and other fiscal support measures to boost consumption.
